text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=service/inference-queue, symptom=queue_depth>5000 for 3m. PagerDuty INC: <https://pagerduty.local/INC-2026-789|INC-2026-789>. Priority: P1. escalation: oncall-sre rotation notified.

pagerduty-bot: page sent to @sandra (primary on-call).

sandra: ack — I'm on it. starting triage. :eyes:

mike: seeing p95 token latency jump 2.1s -> 9.2s, queue_depth ~5.4k, node CPU near 98%, GPU utilization pegged. metrics dashboard: https://grafana/internal/d/inf-queue

jin: logs from scale-controller look odd: "scale-controller: warmup skipped: nodeQuotaExceeded=true" repeated. snippet:```2026-03-15T14:02:11Z scale-controller warn warmup skipped (requested 6 nodes) reason=nodeQuotaExceeded```. autoscaler did not request extra nodes successfully.

devon: cloud console shows region-us-west2 ephemeral GPU quota at 10/10. requests pending. looks like we hit provider quota.

sandra: can we manual spin nodes while we sort quota? will open a provider support ticket but need immediate relief.

mike: suggested quick mitigations: 1) manual node spin up (if allowed), 2) shift some traffic to us-east fallback pool, 3) enable model-fallback (quantized smaller model) to reduce per-request GPU time, 4) throttle non-prod jobs.

devon: manual scale command (running now):
```bash
# create new node pool with n=4 (fallback spot if possible)
cloudcli compute nodepool create --region us-west2 --type gpu-v2 --count 4 --name temp-autoscale-burst
# kubernetes side: increase replicas for inference workers
kubectl scale deployment inference-workers --replicas=30 -n prod
```

ops-bot: spawn-nodes job started id=spawn-9876, provider request submitted. estimated provisioning 3-5m.

mike: routing change: increasing traffic-split for fallback region to 25% to reduce steady pressure here. applying: `routerctl set split inference=us-east:0.25,us-west2:0.75`

jin: customer-side errors: 503s and 429s being observed. sample error log: "{\"time\":\"2026-03-15T14:03:21Z\", \"code\":503, \"path\":\"/v1/generate\", \"msg\":\"server overloaded\"}". CS pinged and monitoring customers with active incidents.

sandra: ok plan of attack: (A) let spawn job complete, (B) enable model-fallback for high-cost models to quantized variants, (C) throttle non-prod by 80%, (D) keep routing change live. devon/jin — coordinate steps B/C. I'll keep command/control.

devon: flipping fallback flag in config service now:```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" https://config.redwood.internal/v1/flags/model_fallback -d '{"enabled":true,"models":["gptx-16q","gptx-8q"]}'``` will monitor effect.

ops-bot: nodes reporting join: node-ug-44,node-ug-45,node-ug-46,node-ug-47. kv-cache warmup triggered for inference shards.

mike: metrics update 14:07Z: queue_depth -> 1.2k, p95 latency -> 2.0s, error rate down from 6% -> 1.4%. customer errors still trickling but improving.

sandra: good. leaving jin on shift to watch next 2h and do post-incident filing. handing off now. please escalate to incidents channel with timeline and logs. :thumbsup:

jin: ack — taking over. I'll create the incident doc and link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-789 and include autoscaler warmup logs, provider quota details, and mitigation timeline. tagging @product for potential rate-limit opt-in on non-prod.

mike: one more note: need follow-up action — add autoscaler retry for quota-limited warmups and a pre-flight provider quota check before scaling decisions.

sandra: agreed. adding to action items. closing this page once jin posts the incident writeup. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
